title: Billing Adjustments, Credit Memo & Invoice Dispute SOP
author: Elena Martinez
body:
Overview

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) describes the end-to-end process for handling billing adjustments, credit memos, and customer invoice disputes. It clarifies ownership, expected timelines, accounting treatment, and controls to ensure accurate revenue recognition and timely customer service. This document applies to all Redwood Inference invoiced customers and internal chargeback corrections.

Scope

- Applies to all hosted, dedicated, and private billing events (usage, reserved capacity, overages, and manual credits).
- Excludes refunds for hardware procurement; hardware/vendor refunds follow procurement SOPs.

Definitions

1) Invoice dispute: A formal challenge by a customer about an invoice line or total.
2) Credit memo: An accounting document issued to reduce receivable/invoice amount.
3) Billing adjustment: Internal change to a posted invoice or account (example: misapplied credits, duplicate charges).
4) AR hold: Temporary suspension of collection while dispute is being investigated.

Responsibilities and RACI

- Customer Success: First-line intake for disputes and communication owner until resolution.
- Billing & Finance (AR team): Owns investigation, approves accounting entries, issues credit memos and posts adjustments.
- Legal: Reviews disputes that meet contract escalation criteria or potential legacy liability.
- Sales/Account Exec: Confirms contract terms and pricing for commercial exceptions.
- Engineering/Platform: Provides usage logs, model-run traces, and config snapshots for technical disputes.

RACI summary:
- Receive dispute: Customer Success (R) / Billing (A)
- Investigate: Billing (R) / Engineering (C) / Sales (C)
- Approve credit: Billing Finance (A) / Legal (C for >$50k or multi-period)
- Issue credit memo: Billing Finance (R/A)
- Post accounting entry: Finance GL Team (R)

SLA Targets

- Acknowledgement to customer: within 24 business hours.
- Initial investigation complete: within 5 business days.
- Resolution (credit issued or decision communicated): within 15 business days for standard disputes.
- Complex/escalated disputes involving contract/legal review: target 30 calendar days.

Intake and Triage (Step-by-step)

1) Intake: Customer opens a ticket via Support Portal or emails billing@redwood.ai. Customer Success creates a Dispute Case in the Billing Disputes queue with the following minimum fields: customer_id, invoice_id, disputed_amount, reason_code (choose from: usage_discrepancy, pricing_error, duplicate_charge, credit_application, tax_issue, other), and supporting documents.

2) Triage by Customer Success (within 24 business hours):
   - Verify receipt and confirm customer contact details.
   - Assign priority code: P1 (>= $50k or business-impacting), P2 ($5k–$50k or product-impacting), P3 (< $5k).
   - For P1/P2, notify Billing & Finance and Sales immediately.

3) Create investigation ticket in Finance case system (NetSuite/Chargebee/AR sub-ledger) and link to Support ticket.

Investigation Checklist (Billing & Finance)

For each dispute, follow these steps and document findings in the finance case record: 

- Step A: Validate invoice data
  - Confirm invoice date, billing period, plan/sku, rate card used, and tax calculation.
  - Verify invoice was generated against customer-specified pricing table and approved contract amendment (if any).

- Step B: Reproduce usage charge (if applicable)
  - Request engineering export: usage_details.csv containing columns: timestamp, model_id, cpu_gpu_seconds, tokens_in, tokens_out, route_id, request_id.
  - Use the following sample SQL to cross-check billed tokens against usage exports:

    SELECT invoice_id, SUM(billed_tokens) as billed_tokens, SUM(actual_tokens) as actual_tokens
    FROM billing_exports
    WHERE customer_id = '<<customer_id>>' AND invoice_period = '<<YYYY-MM>>'
    GROUP BY invoice_id;

- Step C: Check for applied credits or promos
  - Confirm if automatic credits (trial credits, promotional discounts, reserved capacity amortization) were applied.

- Step D: Check for double billing / system error
  - Search for duplicate invoice numbers or repeated job runs within 1 hour of each other.

Approval Matrix and GL Treatment

- Credits under $1,000: Billing Finance Lead approval.
- Credits $1,000–$50,000: Finance Manager + Billing Lead approval.
- Credits >$50,000 or multi-period impact: Finance Director + Legal review required.

Accounting entries (examples):
- Issuing a credit memo that reduces Accounts Receivable (AR):
  - Debit Revenue Reduction (GL 4012)
  - Credit Accounts Receivable (GL 1201)

- If cash was already collected and refund is required:
  - Debit Cash/Bank (GL 1001)
  - Credit AR (GL 1201) and record refund reason code.

Revenue recognition impact

- Short-term billing corrections (credit memo applied within same reporting period as invoice): recognize as contra-revenue in the same period.
- Adjustments that affect prior-period recognized revenue (post-close): require an adjusting journal entry and disclosure per accounting policy. Legal and Finance must be notified; threshold for disclosure: cumulative impact > $250k.

Issuing a Credit Memo

1) Prepare credit memo form in AR system with: credit_memo_id, original_invoice_id, credit_amount, reason_code, approver_id, accounting_impact (GL lines), and memo_text.
2) Attach supporting documents: investigation summary, engineering usage extracts, and customer confirmation message.
3) Post the credit memo and generate PDF copy for customer.
4) Notify Customer Success and Sales that the credit has been issued and update case status to Resolved.

Dispute Escalation to Legal

Escalate to Legal when any of the following criteria are met:
- Potential liability or credits > $50,000.
- Dispute involves contract interpretation (billing term ambiguity, SLA credits claimed beyond standard policy).
- Customer threatens litigation or contract termination.

Legal will:
- Provide formal response templates, evaluate contract language, and recommend hold/settlement terms.

Special Cases and Examples

Example A — Usage discrepancy (customer claims over-billing):
1. Engineering provides request-level logs and token counts for the disputed window.
2. Billing Finance recalculates billed tokens using rate card; discrepancy confirmed = 2% billed overage due to parser bug.
3. Approver signs credit for the prorated overage. Credit memo issued and contra-revenue posted.

Example B — Contracted reserved capacity misapplied:
1. Sales confirms a signed PO for Dedicated capacity with a different amortization start date.
2. Billing identifies 3 months of misapplied usage at on-demand rates.
3. Finance issues credit for differential and adjusts future invoices to reflect correct amortization.

Controls and Audit Trail

- Every credit memo must reference an investigation case id and have at least one supporting document attached.
- Approvals recorded via e-signature or system approval workflow.
- Quarterly audit: Random sample of 10% of credit memos and top-10 credits by dollar value reviewed by Internal Audit and Head of Finance.

Reporting and Metrics

Key metrics maintained in the Billing Dashboard:
- Open disputes (count) and age distribution
- Time to resolution (median and 90th percentile)
- Total credits issued (YTD) and as % of gross billings
- Top 10 dispute reasons by volume and by amount

Sample BigQuery for monthly credits by reason:

SELECT reason_code, COUNT(1) AS disputes, SUM(credit_amount) AS total_credit
FROM `redwood-billing.procedures.credit_memos`
WHERE DATE(issued_at) BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY reason_code
ORDER BY total_credit DESC;

Operational Checklist for Customer Success (closing loop)

1. Confirm customer received credit memo PDF.
2. Confirm invoice status is Updated/Closed in the customer portal.
3. Update renewal or committed capacity calculations if dispute impacts committed usage.

Access, Segregation of Duties, and System Notes

- Billing creation and approval capabilities are separated: AR clerks can draft credit memos but cannot approve above their approval limit.
- Journals that impact prior-period revenue require Director-level signoff.
- System logs retained for 7 years in accordance with retention policy.

Customer Communication Templates (summary)

- Acknowledgement (24h): "We received your dispute for invoice INV-<<id>>. Our team is reviewing and will update you within 5 business days. Case: CASE-<<id>>."
- Resolution with credit: "We issued credit memo CM-<<id>> for $<<amount>>. Attached is the PDF and applied ledger entries. If you have questions, contact billing@redwood.ai."

FAQ (short)

Q: Will a dispute place my account on hold?
A: Only if the dispute is P1 or there is an active AR hold by the finance team. Customer Success will notify you.

Q: Does a credit memo change my contract?
A: No — credit memos correct invoicing or compensate for operational errors; contract terms remain unchanged unless accompanied by a signed amendment.
